title: Identification data for Linear Direct Drive Forces compensation
rights: CC BY 4.0 (DaRUS release-wide). All listed files are public. The repository stores attributed aggregate tables and independent processing code.
evidence_level: usable files; complete release downloaded and checked

queries.query: ("feed drive" OR "ball screw" OR "ballscrew") AND types.resourceTypeGeneral:Dataset

related_sources: The controller comparison on the same test bench explicitly reuses the force map. https://doi.org/10.18419/darus-3109

keys: Identification data for Linear Direct Drive Forces compensation
history.scope: 1141 Git-tracked evidence paths, 301 members inside tar.gz, gzip contents and early baseline-index. Case/punctuation/accents normalized. Paper titles used for replication releases.

methods: Nearest-time pairing of the 1 kHz command grid and 4 kHz measured motor and table signals via dSPACE XIndex. Worst timestamp residual is zero. Checked F_nut_sum against the four individual KISTLER channels where available.

For each uncompensated direction and speed, held out one whole run and trained on the other three speeds in that direction. Kept 0.02 ≤ planned position < 0.70 m, within 1% of commanded cruise speed, and computed median nut force per 10 mm position bin. Compared medians across training speeds with a single median across all training bins; reported equal-bin-weighted test RMSE.

Read the separate Siemens PRBS export using semicolon delimiter and decimal comma. Fit a one-step model of r78[k] as intercept plus r78[k−1] and r77[k−lag]. Searched lag 0–16 on the first half only with a common set of 1,007 training rows; evaluated all 1,024 second-half rows against persistence.
results: All eight uncompensated forward/backward runs at 25, 50, 75 and 100 mm/s show a zero commanded LDD force while nut sensors measure loads up to about 643 N in magnitude. Both compensated validation runs have all four component forces; the arithmetic sum agrees exactly with F_nut_sum on the stored grid.

All eight held-out-speed cases cover 68 common bins. Position-conditioned force RMSE is 2.038–7.192 N, compared with 52.697–55.359 N for the position-independent training median. Same-bench, same-direction repeatability supports disturbance mapping.

The 2,047-sample PRBS trace uses ±19.999996 N requests and 0.0625 ms spacing. Eleven reported actual-force samples exceed the excitation envelope, range −20.397829 to +21.063169 N. A 3-sample input lag minimizes training one-step error; held-out RMSE 1.964 N versus 3.624 N persistence.
limitations: PRBS actual force is inverter-reported r78, with no independent force transducer in that CSV. The KISTLER nut force in the MAT experiments measures a different quantity and may drift according to the author.

The two compensated validation traces run at 10 mm/s. The available uncompensated speeds differ, so a compensation-only causal effect cannot be isolated. The ±20 N PRBS envelope and nominal metadata range ±100 Nm do not establish a physical drive saturation limit. One-step lag is model-specific.

companion_full_text.citation: Christoph Hinze (2023). Dynamiksteigerung von Kugelgewindetrieben durch modellbasierte Lageregelung der nachgiebigen Mechanik. Universität Stuttgart, dissertation.
companion_full_text.evidence: Full text reviewed. Appendix A.3, printed pp. 180–181, specifies Heidenhain LS187C linear readout, separate AM2048S/R motor encoder, and four Kistler 9323A force sensors with 5017B1800 amplifier. The author gives 3 µm specified linear measurement accuracy and 4.88 nm readout resolution. Bibliography item [104] explicitly cites this dataset DOI. Section 6.3, printed pp. 79–82, compares speed-controller settings with the position loop deactivated.
